statement.p: Compute the derivative of the given function in two different ways.
a) Use the Product Rule, [fg]' = f\cdot g' + f' \cdot g. (Fill in each blank, then simplify.)
b) Use algebra first to simplify h, then differentiate without the Product Rule.

static.solution:
Solution:
First, using the Product Rule,
\begin{array}{rcl} h'(s) \amp =\amp (-5 s + 4) \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[ 7 s - 3 ] + \frac{d}{dx}[ -5 s + 4 ] (7 s - 3)\\ \amp \amp \\ \amp =\amp (-5 s + 4)(7) + (-5)(7 s - 3) \\ \end{array} After simplifying the last line, we find h'(s) = -70 s + 43.
Next, simplify h first. Then take the derivative. \begin{array}{rcl} h(s) \amp =\amp (-5 s + 4)(7 s - 3) = -35 s^2 + 43 s - 12 \\ \amp \amp \\ h'(s) \amp =\amp -70 s + 43 \end{array} The two simplified answers should match.
